The Federal Republic of Cameroon was a federal state that emerged on 1 October 1961 from the merger of the Republic of Cameroon (formerly French Cameroon) and Southern Cameroons (formerly part of the British Cameroons). The existence of the two Cameroons is the profound and a major consequence of World War I, which took place on Cameroonian soil and split it up.
It lived from 1 October 1961 to 20 May 1972, and was comprised of two federated states:
* Eastern Cameroon (formerly the Republic of Cameroon), and;
* Western Cameroon (formerly Southern Cameroons, formerly part of the British Cameroons).
History
Independence and merging
On 1 January 1960, French Cameroun gained independence from France under President Ahmadou Ahidjo as the Republic of Cameroon.
On 1 October 1961, the formerly British Southern Cameroons gained independence from the United Kingdom by vote of the UN General Assembly and merged into the Republic of Cameroon to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon. The federal republic was composed of two federated states, East Cameroon and West Cameroon, each with its own legislature, government, and prime minister. 1 October is now observed as Unification Day, a public holiday.
